entities.summary:
Muḥyī al‐Milla wa al‐Dīn Yaḥyā Abū ʿAbdallāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī al‐Shukr al‐Maghribī al‐Andalusī, referred to in sources as Muhyi l'din, was an astronomer, astrologer and mathematician of the Islamic Golden Age. He belonged to the group of astronomers associated with the Maragheh observatory in the Ilkhanate, most notably Nasir al-Din al-Tusi.

 In astronomy, Muhyi l'din carried out a large‐scale project of systematic planetary observations, which led to the development of several new astronomic tables and the creation of a comprehensive system for calculating eclipses. His work was instrumental in establishing the accuracy of astronomical predictions and had a lasting impact on the field of astrology.

 Muhyi l'din's contributions extended beyond his observational work, as he also made significant advancements in mathematical astronomy, including the calculation of planetary orbits and the development of new methods for predicting celestial events. His research and publications were widely respected during his lifetime and continue to be studied by scholars today.

 The significance of Muhyi l'din's work cannot be overstated, particularly in the context of the Islamic Golden Age, where he played a crucial role in advancing our understanding of the universe. His contributions to astronomy and mathematics had far-reaching consequences, influencing the development of science and civilization for centuries to come.

 As we reflect on Muhyi l'din's legacy, it is clear that his work represents a pivotal moment in the history of human knowledge, one that continues to inspire new generations of scholars and scientists.

entities.summary:
Muḥyī al‐Milla wa al‐Dīn Yaḥyā Abū ʿAbdallāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī al‐Shukr al‐Maghribī al‐Andalusī, referred to in sources as Muhyi l'din, was an astronomer, astrologer and mathematician of the Islamic Golden Age.

 Born in 1220 in al-Andalus, he belonged to the group of astronomers associated with the Maragheh observatory in the Ilkhanate, most notably Nasir al-Din al-Tusi. In astronomy, Muhyi l'din carried out a large‐scale project of systematic planetary observations.

 This led to the development of several new astronomical tables and models, which were later used by other scholars such as Ulugh Beg in Samarkand. The significance of Muhyi l'din's work lies in its contribution to the field of astronomy during the Islamic Golden Age, and its impact on the development of astronomy in Europe.

 His work also reflects the cultural exchange between East and West during this period, with influences from Arabic, Persian and Turkish scholars.

 The legacy of Muhyi l'din can be seen in the continued use of his astronomical tables by later scholars, and his influence on the development of astronomy in the Ottoman Empire.

 'The heavenly bodies are the seats of divine authority', Muhyi l'din wrote, reflecting the deep reverence for astronomy in Islamic tradition. \
